obligation: CISA cybersecurity incident report (Covered Railroads)
trigger: Cybersecurity incident on IT or OT systems the railroad operates or maintains: unauthorized access, malicious software, denial of service, or other incident with actual or potential operational disruption (includes events still under investigation)
deadline: As soon as practicable and no later than 72 hours after identification (company target: 24 hours)
notify: CISA Central: www.cisa.gov/report or (844) 729-2472; the report must say it is made to satisfy the SD

obligation: CISA supplemental information
trigger: Required report content not available at the initial report
deadline: Within 24 hours of the information becoming available

obligation: TSA Transportation Security Operations Center notice (recommended)
citation: IC Surface-2025-01 (voluntary), as described in FR Doc. 2026-17894
trigger: Actual or potential significant cybersecurity incident
deadline: As soon as possible and no more than 12 hours after discovery (recommendation, not a mandate)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company practice for all 64 railroads

obligation: TSA report of significant security concerns
citation: 49 CFR 1570.203(a)-(c); Appendix A to part 1570 ("Cyber Attack")
trigger: Potential threat or significant security concern, including a cyber attack, on any company railroad
deadline: Within 24 hours of initial discovery; a CISA report under the SD that says so satisfies 1570.203 for the same incident (SD 1580-21-01E Sec. II.C.5)
notify: TSA by the methods TSA prescribes (TSOC)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all 64 railroads (separate TSA report for the 54 not covered by the SD report)

obligation: TSA RSSM location request during an outage
trigger: TSA asks for RSSM car location and shipping information
deadline: No later than 30 minutes after the request (not Class I)

obligation: TSA notice when an SD measure cannot be implemented
citation: SD 1580-21-01E Sec. III.C and Sec. V; SD 1580/82-2022-01E Sec. II.B.2 (CIP measures)
trigger: The incident or recovery makes the railroad unable to implement an SD or CIP measure within the required time
deadline: Immediately
notify: TSA at SurfOpsRail-SD@tsa.dhs.gov or TSA-Surface-Cyber@tsa.dhs.gov as the SD directs
clock_starts: Determination that a measure cannot be met

obligation: SSI released to unauthorized persons
trigger: Attackers or others obtain SSI (for example, the CIP, zone designs, or incident reports)
deadline: Promptly

obligation: PTC en route failure report to the host railroad
trigger: PTC back office or onboard failure or cut-out while en route
deadline: As soon as safe and practicable
notify: Designated officer of the host railroad (the company itself for CR-07 to CR-09; the Class I host for tenant moves)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - CR-07 to CR-09 and 22 tenant railroads

obligation: FRA notice of PTC safety-relevant failures over PTCSP thresholds
trigger: Frequency of a safety-relevant hazard exceeds the PTCSP threshold, or a failure decreases safety functionality
deadline: Within 15 days after discovery
notify: FRA (Associate Administrator) and the PTC vendor
clock_starts: Discovery of the failure or defective condition

obligation: FRA telephonic accident report
trigger: An accident or incident meeting 225.9(a) occurs during degraded operations (for example, a fatality, or a train accident fouling a passenger main line)
deadline: Immediately
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all 64 railroads (only if such an accident occurs)

obligation: Maritime cyber incident report
trigger: Actual or threatened cyber incident involving or endangering a port or waterfront facility where the 2 port switching railroads work
deadline: Immediately
notify: FBI, CISA, and the Captain of the Port; also the facility security officer by agreement
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, in part - 2 port switching railroads

obligation: SEC materiality determination
trigger: Any cybersecurity incident that may be material
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery
notify: Disclosure committee (internal decision, recorded with date and time)

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing
trigger: Incident determined to be material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: The U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Delay only for the period the Attorney General specifies
notify: Department of Justice through outside counsel

obligation: SEC annual cybersecurity disclosure
trigger: Annual report
deadline: With the Form 10-K

obligation: Insider trading blackout
trigger: Severity-1 incident under review by the disclosure committee
deadline: At once on the committee's first meeting
notify: Committee members, responders with knowledge, executives

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of personal information as each state defines it (for example, employee SSNs, certification and medical records)
deadline: Varies by state: without unreasonable delay or a fixed number of days; use the earliest applicable deadline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - employees and former employees in 27 operating states and elsewhere
clock_starts: Discovery or determination of the breach, as each state defines it

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above the count set by each state
deadline: Varies by state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - where state counts are met

obligation: State consumer reporting agency notice
trigger: Breach above the count set by each state
deadline: Varies by state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - where state counts are met

obligation: State third-party agent (vendor) notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that holds company personal information has a breach
deadline: Varies by state; contracts require 10 days or sooner
notify: The company (Director of Third-Party Risk Management)

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security affecting personal information of Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determining a breach occurred or having reason to believe one occurred; up to 15 more days on good cause given in writing to the Department within 30 days (501.171(3)(a); this extension applies only to the individual notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Florida employees and former employees
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (no 15-day extension)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: More than 1,000 individuals notified at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (worked example)
trigger: A third-party agent holding company data has a breach
deadline: As soon as practicable and no later than 10 days after determining the breach

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any proposal to pay a ransom
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA

obligation: Law enforcement report (voluntary)
trigger: Ransomware or extortion
deadline: As early as practicable

obligation: CIRCIA covered incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Would apply to covered entities once the final rule takes effect
deadline: Not in effect (statute: 72 hours for covered incidents, 24 hours for ransom payments, only after the final rule)
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25

obligation: Cyber insurance notice
trigger: Any incident that may lead to a claim
deadline: Per policy (as soon as practicable; carrier hotline first)

obligation: SL-1 and SL-2 customer notice
trigger: Incident affecting customer service or data
deadline: Within 24 hours of declaration for service impact; status every 4 hours until restored

obligation: Class I and passenger operator notice
citation: Interchange, trackage rights, and operating agreements
trigger: Loss of dispatch, PTC messaging, or interchange data
deadline: At once by the NOC dispatcher-to-dispatcher line; written notice per agreement
notify: Class I dispatch centers; Amtrak and the commuter railroad operations centers

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Discovery during an incident of covered telecommunications equipment in a system used under a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts (recheck if one is signed)

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
trigger: Discovery of a covered article in a system used under a federal contract
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts (recheck if one is signed)
